correctness.rationale: The exact polar identities were derived by Cartesian multiplication and tested symbolically for four orders. At integer order one, the logarithmic-radius angular equation has an explicit strict supersolution ruling out successive late half-turn crossings, giving finite total turning and a limiting horizontal ray. For integer orders at least two, the positive quartic-radius angular contribution has divergent time integral. The frozen full-turn integral equals \(2\pi/[r^3\sqrt{c(b+cr^2)}]\). Over one full turn the radius has relative change \(O(r^{2k-3})\), yielding the exact limiting inverse-radius-power increment \(2\pi(2k-3)a/\sqrt{bc}\). Cesaro averaging establishes the sharp original-time winding limit for every nonzero initial point and positive coefficients. Finite numerical tests supplement, but cannot establish, the infinite-time statements.

value.rationale: A sharp topological boundary arises within a motivated parameterized polynomial family where all trajectories share radial attraction and strictly positive angular velocity. The order-one counterexample shows no-zero-angular-speed curves alone does not force monodromy; from order two onward a full winding law has an exact parameter-dependent constant. The physical-time law explains increasing delay near two angular bottlenecks and yields quartic nth-turn delays at order two, providing a useful explicit test family for interpreting analytic monodromy assumptions rather than an arbitrary finite slice or renaming.
